title: Move instead of copy
description:
Copying a `Buffer` duplicates its whole array. When the source is a temporary that is about to be destroyed anyway, that is wasted work: the new object can simply **take** the array.

Add the two move operations to `Buffer`:

- move constructor `Buffer(Buffer&& other) noexcept`: take `other`'s pointer and size, and leave `other` empty (null pointer, size 0);
- move assignment `Buffer& operator=(Buffer&& other) noexcept`: free your own array, then take `other`'s the same way. Guard against self-move.

`std::exchange(a, b)` sets `a` to `b` and returns the old value of `a`, which makes "take it and leave null behind" a one-liner.
hints: The move constructor takes the resources in its initializer list: `m_data{ std::exchange(other.m_data, nullptr) }, m_size{ std::exchange(other.m_size, 0) }`.
Move assignment: if `this != &other`, `delete[]` your own array, then take `other`'s with the same two `std::exchange` calls, and `return *this;`.
